editorial:
Imagine a world where fancy suits meet gritty street crime, and everyone is trying to outsmart each other. You follow Mickey Pearson, a smooth American who built a massive weed business in London. He just wants to retire and sell his empire, but that news starts a chaotic chain reaction. You get a mix of scary gangsters, greedy politicians, and a sneaky private investigator who tries to blackmail his way to the top. The whole vibe is stylish, loud, and full of sharp dialogue that keeps you laughing while the tension builds up.

What really makes this work is the acting and the way the story jumps around. The twists are clever and the pacing never slows down, so you won't find yourself checking your phone. While some of the plots get a bit tangled, the payoff is totally worth it. If you love crime capers, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a huge showdown where the bad guys think they have won. However, Mickey and his team were actually one step ahead the whole time. They set a trap that wipes out the rivals and secures Mickey's business. The private investigator gets outsmarted and loses his leverage. In the end, Mickey keeps his empire and his wealth, proving that he is the smartest person in the room.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever crime stories and witty banter.
similarMovies: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
